summary: Priority-weight transition lag results in background-flushes consuming burst credits and causing early 429s for interactive routes
description:
Issue summary:
SkylineChat reports repeated early 429s affecting low-latency chat routes after their account was promoted to an enterprise plan with higher burst credits. The tenant experiences normal throughput for bulk/background flush jobs but interactive SSE/chat endpoints begin receiving 429s within minutes of the promotion.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429s on interactive chat routes (SSE & websocket) causing degraded real-time UX for SkylineChat customers.
- Bulk ingestion (background flushers) shows increased token consumption and appears to be draining burst credits during the transition window.
- Customer reports business impact: chat sessions dropping for end-users during peak business hours.

Environment:
- Tenant: SkylineChat (enterprise)
- Region: prod-us-west primary, spillover to eu-west reported
- Models: redwood-2-large for chat, redwood-1-quantized for background encode
- Config: priority-split enabled with separate lanes for interactive (high) and background (low) traffic; recently changed weight thresholds as part of onboarding.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Promote tenant plan to enterprise (increase burst credits + priority weights)
2) System kicks off background flushes to catch up (many short-lived parallel workers)
3) Within ~3-7 minutes interactive connections begin seeing 429 responses
4) Token accounting shows large sink from background workers attributed to the same tenant during the transition window

Observed behavior (logs/metrics):
- Ingress rate-limiter traces show priority_ladder transition event at 2026-03-08T14:02:11Z then a burst of low-priority background-worker calls between 14:02:12Z-14:09:00Z.
- Example token-accounting line (edge logs):
  [2026-03-08T14:04:37Z] tenant=skylinechat route=/v1/generate tokens=23872 worker=flush-coordinator-22 priority=LOW counted=true
  [2026-03-08T14:04:38Z] tenant=skylinechat route=/v1/chat tokens=12 session=abc123 priority=HIGH result=429 reason=quota_exhausted
- Rate-limiter debug shows window refill event delayed by ~45s after promotion due to epoch swap on rate-controller nodes.
- Prometheus metrics: rate_limit_token_pool_available{tenant="skylinechat"} dropped from ~120k to <4k in the transition window; background_worker_token_rate spiked x8.

Expected behavior:
- Priority promotions should not allow background flushers to siphon newly-allocated burst credits before interactive lanes get rebalanced; interactive sessions should be prioritized during and immediately after plan change.

Temporary mitigations attempted by Support/Customer:
- Customer paused background flushers (reduced worker parallelism) which restored interactive success within ~30s.
- Support toggled a temporary soft-isolate flag that pins interactive routes to a protected burst pool; prevented further 429s for the duration.

Investigation notes and hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Rate-controller epoch exchange during tier update causes a short window where refill assignments are not synchronized across origin and edge, allowing background workers to claim new credits first.
- Hypothesis B: Priority weight recalculation happens asynchronously; background lane retains older token slice until the weight update completes, resulting in effective over-allocation to background workers.
- Hypothesis C: Orchestrator warms up many parallel short-lived flush workers after promotion; our per-route token attribution (edge-side) misattributes some of those against interactive route token pools when path normalization occurs (signed-url/callbacks).

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering (rate-limiter team) to reproduce epoch-swap refill lag in staging using the plan-promotion script; create a deterministic integration test reproducing the race. (assigned: Diego)
- Add short-term guard: when a tenant plan changes, apply a 120s protected window that favors interactive lanes for refill allocation. (owner: rate-limiter)
- Add logging around refill assignment decisions and add metric: refill_lag_seconds per-tenant. (owner: telemetry)
- Consolidate runbook steps for customers performing plan upgrades to reduce parallelism of background workers during the first 5 minutes. (owner: customer-success)

Workaround provided to customer:
- Recommended action: pause background flush worker pool and resume gradually with concurrency capped at 2 for the first 5 minutes post promotion.
- Support applied a temporary route-protect flag while engineering works on the long-term fix.

Attachments / evidence:
- rate-limiter traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rate-limiter/tenant-skylinechat/trace-2026-03-08
- support convo: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123ABCDE/p1678643200

Resolution notes: (in progress)
- Short-term protective guard implemented as tenant flag (rollout candidate) and tested in staging.
- Root-cause reproduction pending; target for patch and global rollout: 2026-03-20.
